thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: SEV2 serving degradation in us-east-1 (auto-detect: packet-loss > 5% across RDMA fabric)
maya (oncall): I'm on it. seeing a spike in request latencies and some CUDA OOMs on rack-3 nodes.
sam (infra): noticed IB retransmit counters climbing on 3 nodes (node-43, node-44, node-45). mlx5 driver flapping in dmesg.
dinesh (runtime): logs show container restarts with `CUDA error: out of memory` around the same time. suspect KV-cache misses + retransmits causing backpressure.
kevin (sre): marking as paged. tagging customers who hit 503s in last 10m.
maya (oncall): quick mitigations: 1) move traffic off rack-3 2) reduce per-request batch size 3) enable fallback model on cpu for low-priority routes.
emma (support): I have affected customer list from the alert, will prep comms if we need an incident banner.
sam (infra): running `ethtool -S ib0` shows tx_retries and rx_errors high on node-44. also see IB path manager flaps:
```
[ 12345.678901] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: mlx5_ib: hotpluggable port 1 changed
[ 12345.679012] mlx5_core 0000:03:00.0: ibdev1: port 1 link down
```
dinesh (runtime): for immediate relief can we drain node-44 and restart the serving container? i'll prepare a reduced-config image to restart without kvcache (fast path) to avoid large memory pressure.
maya (oncall): doing `kubectl cordon node-44` now.
kevin (sre): heads up, if we mass-evacuate pods we might spike overload on remaining nodes. recommend gradual cordon + redirect route weight.
maya (oncall): using rollout-script to shift 30% traffic off rack-3: `./scripts/route-weight --from rack-3 --to rack-1 --pct 30`
sam (infra): node-44 cordoned. starting `systemctl restart mlx5` equivalent (driver reload) on node-44. will watch link.
dinesh (runtime): lowering max_batch_size from 8 -> 4 in config and bumping request-timeout to 8s for affected model. applying canary to 2 pods.
kevin (sre): anomaly detection shows packet loss drop after first 10m but latency still high. any CUDA OOMs after cordon?
maya (oncall): OOMs stopped on node-44 after restart and traffic shift. node-43 still showing intermittent IB retransmit bursts.
sam (infra): collecting kdump and `dmesg | tail -n 50` from node-43, pushing to /tmp/inc-3723456789-logs
```
# dmesg excerpt
[ 54321.123456] Kernel panic - not syncing: watchdog
[ 54321.123460] Evicted memory resources
```
emma (support): customer impact: 12 enterprise customers saw elevated 5xx rates, 3 reported production failures. preparing status update draft.
dinesh (runtime): plan for next 30m: fully evacuate rack-3 if retransmits persist; enable CPU fallback for low-priority routings; open a hardware ticket for NICs on node-43/45.
maya (oncall): handing off to night oncall (sam) in 15m. leaving runbook steps and current mitigations. pinging sam for takeover.
sam (infra): taking handoff. outlined next steps in thread and creating follow-up ticket INC-3723456789 for hardware replacement + postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident INC-3723456789 created and assigned to infra/sre. Priority SEV2.
emma (support): posting customer-facing note to status page (draft) and emailing affected contacts now.
kevin (sre): reminder to include telemetry: packet loss graphs, dmesg snippets, last good commit, and rollout timeline in postmortem.
maya (oncall): thanks team. root cause hypothesis: intermittent IB link-level flaps causing retransmits, which amplified KV-cache misses and runtime memory pressure leading to CUDA OOMs and container restarts. will confirm with hardware vendor logs.
sam (infra): monitoring continues. I'll update on progress; leaving pager unack if things re-escalate.
